title: "A Docker image without the which command keeps R from starting"
ref: ENV-03
categories: [OS and CI]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "R starting normally in the rocker/verse image"
versions: "rocker/verse images based on Ubuntu Jammy, in October 2023"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2023)"
---

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```yaml
# .gitlab-ci.yml
image: rocker/verse:latest

check:
  script:
    - R -e 'devtools::check()'
```
:::

This pitfall depends on the contents of a Docker image at a given date, so it cannot be replayed in the browser.

## Why

The `R` launcher is a shell script, which relies on system commands to locate its own components. In October 2023, the latest `rocker/verse` image, based on Ubuntu Jammy, no longer contained the `which` command, provided by the `debianutils` system package.

R then could not find its base packages, `base`, `utils`, `stats`, and the pipeline stopped on startup errors that never mentioned `which`. Images based on Ubuntu Focal, such as `rocker/verse:4.1`, worked.

## The remedy

Pin a tested image version rather than `latest`, as the team did by going back to a Focal-based image, and check that `which` is there before launching R.

::: {.piege .piege-statique}
```yaml
image: rocker/verse:4.1.2

before_script:
  - command -v which
```
:::
